subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` be treated as an enforced per-DM security boundary, or should OpenClaw retire/clarify that accepted config surface?
rationale: The config/schema already accepts a security-sensitive policy knob, but runtime does not enforce it on direct-message sessions; automation cannot safely choose between enforcing a shipped-looking boundary and removing or documenting it as unsupported.

options.title: Enforce direct tools policy
options.body: Implement direct/DM-aware tool-policy resolution for Telegram with account-specific, wildcard, thread/topic, and `toolsBySender` precedence preserved, plus regression and live-channel proof.

options.title: Retire or clarify the surface
options.body: Remove or explicitly mark `direct.*.tools` unsupported and provide any needed doctor/docs migration so operators do not rely on a false security boundary.

options.title: Fold into broader binding policy
options.body: Defer this fix only if maintainers choose one unified conversation/binding policy model that covers this Telegram direct case without leaving the accepted config silently ignored.

recommendation.title: Enforce direct tools policy
recommendation.body: Implement direct/DM-aware tool-policy resolution for Telegram with account-specific, wildcard, thread/topic, and `toolsBySender` precedence preserved, plus regression and live-channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared tool-policy scope work and security hardening make this the best available owner for the enforcement-vs-retirement decision.
